holidays.name: Be a Millionaire Day
holidays.description: A daydream-friendly day for imagining your bank balance with a lot more zeros. People celebrate by brainstorming big money ideas, setting savings goals, or pretending to shop like a tycoon.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on fun-holiday calendars as a prompt to think big about money.
holidays.funFact: If you saved $1 a day, it would take you more than 2,700 years to reach a million dollars, so compound interest and a good plan help a lot.

holidays.name: Eliza Doolittle Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the flower girl who learns to speak like a lady. Celebrate by practicing your poshest accent, watching My Fair Lady, or trying to say the rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the heroine of George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion and the musical My Fair Lady.
holidays.funFact: The 1964 film My Fair Lady won eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

holidays.name: World Metrology Day (Weights and Measures Day)
holidays.description: A salute to the science of measurement, which keeps your kilos, litres and kilometres consistent around the world. It's a good day to appreciate rulers, scales and measuring cups.
holidays.origin: The date marks the signing of the Metre Convention in Paris on May 20, 1875. That treaty created an international system for standardized measurement.
holidays.funFact: For many decades the kilogram was defined by a physical metal cylinder kept in France. It was redefined in 2019 using a fixed constant of nature instead.
